results.notes: verifyEvent from nostr-tools/pure on every EVENT (id = sha256 of JSON.stringify serialization, then schnorr.verify); its verified-symbol cache is a property of each parsed event object, so it never carries across events or runs. matchFilters runs on every event. Subscription eoseTimeout raised to --timeout-ms: its default (relay.baseEoseTimeout, 4400 ms) starts at the REQ and fakes an EOSE when it fires, which a slow verifier streaming 31k events would hit long before the real EOSE.

results.notes: nostr-tools' documented fast verifier (its README: "nostr-tools/wasm" for faster verification), its own client entry per HARNESS.md "Fairness". The documented nostr-tools/wasm setup: setNostrWasm(await initNostrWasm()) and an AbstractRelay with the wasm verifyEvent (id recomputed from a JS serialization and hashed in wasm, compared to event.id, then schnorrsig_verify). Subscription eoseTimeout raised to --timeout-ms: its default (relay.baseEoseTimeout, 4400 ms) starts at the REQ and fakes an EOSE when it fires, which a slow verifier streaming 31k events would hit long before the real EOSE.

results.api: new NDK({explicitRelayUrls}) + ndk.connect(), ndk.subscribe(filter, {}, {onEvent, onEose})
results.notes: NDK samples verification: initialValidationRatio and lowestValidationRatio set to 1 so every event is verified (defaults 1 and 0.1: the ratio decays toward 0.1 as a relay sends valid events). NDKEvent.verifySignature checks the schnorr signature against the hash it recomputes from the event, but never compares that hash to event.id, so the harness also calls the library's own ndkEvent.getEventHash() and drops events whose id differs (inside the timed run; it re-serializes and re-hashes, a second sha256 per event). NDK caches verification results by id in a process-global LRU (verifiedSignatures: 1000 ids, 60 s) that is not exported: on a workload of up to 1000 events every run after the first would skip verification. The harness reaches it once in load() (untimed: LRUCache.prototype.set wrapped for a single verifySignature call on a dummy event, then restored) and clears it in every teardown. Outbox model and user-relay autoconnect off (one relay: they would dial public relays). Subscription options are the defaults (live subscription, groupable with its 10 ms grouping delay, no cache adapter). A new NDK instance per run; connect() waits for the relay.

results.crypto: nostr-wasm 0.1.0 (libsecp256k1 in WebAssembly) via @welshman/util verifyEvent → nostr-tools/wasm
results.notes: welshman at its fastest configuration (ranked; the `welshman` row is the default configuration): its send and receive queue delays off through the public static settings. By default every Socket sends through a TaskQueue that waits Socket.sendBatchDelay (100 ms, a setTimeout) before each batch, so the REQ leaves 100 ms after request(), and hands inbound messages to subscribers through a TaskQueue of recvBatchSize 20 per recvBatchDelay 100 ms, so a socket delivers at most ~200 messages per second whatever the CPU; here Socket.sendBatchDelay = 0 and Socket.recvBatchDelay = 0 (the queues then drain on a microtask), which leaves the cost of the parsing, verification and bookkeeping. Otherwise as the welshman row (nostr-tools/wasm verifier confirmed in load(); Tracker dedup, matchFilters and the result array on every event, unconditional).

results.api: new Relay(url), relay.subscription(filter).subscribe({next}) (rxjs; emits events and "EOSE")
results.websocket: rxjs webSocket over the Node global WebSocket (undici)
results.notes: applesauce-relay delivers events unverified (verification belongs to applesauce-core's EventStore); the harness calls applesauce-core/helpers verifyEvent (nostr-tools/pure: id + signature) on each event. The rxjs WebSocketSubject connects lazily on the first subscription, so the connect is inside the timed run (~1 ms on loopback). A new Relay per run. The applesauce app path (relay → EventStore.add, which verifies and indexes) is not a row: a store is outside the job. When it was tested, applesauce-core's EventStore dropped expired events (keepExpired false by default) except one whose expiration tag is "0": it tests the timestamp for truthiness, so 0 reads as no expiration.

results.api: createRxNostr({verifier, skipFetchNip11, skipValidateFilterMatching}) + setDefaultRelays([url]), rxNostr.use(createRxBackwardReq()).subscribe({next, complete}); req.emit(filter); req.over()
results.notes: createRxNostr requires a verifier; the standard one is @rx-nostr/crypto's verifier (async, on the main thread). It checks the signature against the hash it recomputes and never compares it to event.id, so the harness also calls @rx-nostr/crypto getEventHash(event) and drops events whose id differs (a second serialization + sha256 per event). @rx-nostr/crypto verify() calls console.warn with a stack trace for every event whose signature does not parse (the "sig":"" events): console.warn is silenced in this process. rx-nostr drops expired (NIP-40) events by default (skipExpirationCheck: false). The backward request completes on EOSE: completion is the EOSE delivered to the app. eoseTimeout raised to --timeout-ms (default 30 s: it would complete a slow stream early). connectionStrategy "aggressive" + a wait for the relay state "connected" puts the connect in setup. skipFetchNip11: true (documented option; by default each relay connection starts a NIP-11 fetch and the first REQ of a process waits for it, to read max_subscriptions) and skipValidateFilterMatching: true (documented option; by default every event is matched against the REQ filter again). A new rxNostr per run.

results.api: new NostrSystem({checkSigs: true}) + ConnectToRelay(url), system.Query(RequestBuilder.withOptions({leaveOpen: true, groupingDelay: 0}).withFilter().limit(n)).on("event"/"eose"), query.start()
results.notes: NostrSystem does not verify by default (checkSigs: false); the harness turns checkSigs on. Request options: groupingDelay: 0 (the option snort's own fetch() sets; by default Query.start waits groupingDelay = 100 ms on a setTimeout before it sends the REQ, to merge requests) and leaveOpen: true (the query is closed in teardown): with the default (false) a 30 s QueryFetchTimeout hard timer would cut a long stream, and the trace closes at the EOSE while the last events of the socket read that carried it still wait in the pool's queueMicrotask verify batch, so those are dropped (a tail of ~50 events lost, a different number every run). ConnectToRelay does not wait for the socket to open; setup waits until the pool's connection reports isOpen, so the handshake is untimed. Each connection also starts a NIP-11 fetch at connect (in parallel with the handshake, kept in a module-level cache). Unconditional library work: the Query delivers through its feed, a NoteCollection, a sorted in-memory store (a SortedMap insert with splice per event) that hands new events to "event" listeners on a timer (emitInterval 300 ms), so events reach the app up to 300 ms after the EOSE and the run ends at the last one. That store keeps one event per replaceable key (an older kind 0/3/1xxxx version is never delivered) and adds an event only if created_at > (stored.created_at ?? 0), so an event with created_at 0 is never delivered: on the corpus it drops valid events (accepted_ok false). The connection pool batches the events of one microtask turn into one optimizer.batchVerify call; verification checks the signature against an id it recomputes (EventExt.createId) but never compares it to event.id, so the harness also calls EventExt.createId(event) and drops events whose id differs (a second serialization + sha256 per event). "event" handlers receive arrays of new events. Other options default (the automatic outbox model only acts on filters with authors). A new NostrSystem per run. The published dist has extensionless relative ESM imports: on Node the harness registers a module-resolution hook (snort-resolve.mjs: retries .js and /index.js, as a bundler does) to load the unmodified package; Bun resolves them itself; Deno cannot load it.

results.notes: Slow pass: one timed run (no warmup for Dart, JVM and Ruby), in the same batch as the other rows. Library defaults (the default-configuration row; welshman-nodelay is the ranked speed configuration), including the Socket send and receive queues: the REQ itself waits in the send queue for Socket.sendBatchDelay (100 ms, a setTimeout before each batch of sendBatchSize 5), inside the timed run, and inbound messages reach subscribers through a TaskQueue of recvBatchSize 20 per recvBatchDelay 100 ms, i.e. at most ~200 messages/s per socket, so this row is bound by those timers, not the CPU. On Deno, @welshman/util cannot be imported as is (its module-load proof-of-work benchmark starts a classic Worker, which Deno rejects), so the harness hides globalThis.Worker during the import. @welshman/util verifyEvent: nostr-tools/pure until nostr-wasm finishes loading (it imports it dynamically at module load), then nostr-tools/wasm (id + signature); load() waits until a probe confirms the wasm verifier is the one in use and fails otherwise. Unconditional library work on every event: the request Tracker (dedup by id), matchFilters, and the request's result array (request() resolves with the deduplicated list). A new Pool per run (context.pool), socket opened in setup.

results.notes: Library defaults (the default-configuration row; welshman-nodelay is the ranked speed configuration), including the Socket send and receive queues: the REQ itself waits in the send queue for Socket.sendBatchDelay (100 ms, a setTimeout before each batch of sendBatchSize 5), inside the timed run, and inbound messages reach subscribers through a TaskQueue of recvBatchSize 20 per recvBatchDelay 100 ms, i.e. at most ~200 messages/s per socket, so this row is bound by those timers, not the CPU. On Deno, @welshman/util cannot be imported as is (its module-load proof-of-work benchmark starts a classic Worker, which Deno rejects), so the harness hides globalThis.Worker during the import. @welshman/util verifyEvent: nostr-tools/pure until nostr-wasm finishes loading (it imports it dynamically at module load), then nostr-tools/wasm (id + signature); load() waits until a probe confirms the wasm verifier is the one in use and fails otherwise. Unconditional library work on every event: the request Tracker (dedup by id), matchFilters, and the request's result array (request() resolves with the deduplicated list). A new Pool per run (context.pool), socket opened in setup.

results.api: Socket.sendBatchDelay = 0 and Socket.recvBatchDelay = 0, then request({relays: [url], filters: [filter], context: {pool}, onEvent, onEose})
results.crypto: nostr-wasm 0.1.0 (libsecp256k1 in WebAssembly) via @welshman/util verifyEvent → nostr-tools/wasm
results.notes: welshman at its fastest configuration (ranked; the `welshman` row is the default configuration): its send and receive queue delays off through the public static settings. By default every Socket sends through a TaskQueue that waits Socket.sendBatchDelay (100 ms, a setTimeout) before each batch, so the REQ leaves 100 ms after request(), and hands inbound messages to subscribers through a TaskQueue of recvBatchSize 20 per recvBatchDelay 100 ms, so a socket delivers at most ~200 messages per second whatever the CPU; here Socket.sendBatchDelay = 0 and Socket.recvBatchDelay = 0 (the queues then drain on a microtask), which leaves the cost of the parsing, verification and bookkeeping. Otherwise as the welshman row (nostr-tools/wasm verifier confirmed in load(); Tracker dedup, matchFilters and the result array on every event, unconditional).

results.api: new Relay(url), relay.subscription(filter).subscribe({next}) (rxjs; emits events and "EOSE")
results.websocket: rxjs webSocket over the Node global WebSocket (undici)
results.notes: applesauce-relay delivers events unverified (verification belongs to applesauce-core's EventStore); the harness calls applesauce-core/helpers verifyEvent (nostr-tools/pure: id + signature) on each event. The rxjs WebSocketSubject connects lazily on the first subscription, so the connect is inside the timed run (~1 ms on loopback). A new Relay per run. The applesauce app path (relay → EventStore.add, which verifies and indexes) is not a row: a store is outside the job. When it was tested, applesauce-core's EventStore dropped expired events (keepExpired false by default) except one whose expiration tag is "0": it tests the timestamp for truthiness, so 0 reads as no expiration.

results.api: createRxNostr({verifier, skipFetchNip11, skipValidateFilterMatching}) + setDefaultRelays([url]), rxNostr.use(createRxBackwardReq()).subscribe({next, complete}); req.emit(filter); req.over()
results.notes: createRxNostr requires a verifier; the standard one is @rx-nostr/crypto's verifier (async, on the main thread). It checks the signature against the hash it recomputes and never compares it to event.id, so the harness also calls @rx-nostr/crypto getEventHash(event) and drops events whose id differs (a second serialization + sha256 per event). @rx-nostr/crypto verify() calls console.warn with a stack trace for every event whose signature does not parse (the "sig":"" events): console.warn is silenced in this process. rx-nostr drops expired (NIP-40) events by default (skipExpirationCheck: false). The backward request completes on EOSE: completion is the EOSE delivered to the app. eoseTimeout raised to --timeout-ms (default 30 s: it would complete a slow stream early). connectionStrategy "aggressive" + a wait for the relay state "connected" puts the connect in setup. skipFetchNip11: true (documented option; by default each relay connection starts a NIP-11 fetch and the first REQ of a process waits for it, to read max_subscriptions) and skipValidateFilterMatching: true (documented option; by default every event is matched against the REQ filter again). A new rxNostr per run.

results.api: new NostrSystem({checkSigs: true}) + ConnectToRelay(url), system.Query(RequestBuilder.withOptions({leaveOpen: true, groupingDelay: 0}).withFilter().limit(n)).on("event"/"eose"), query.start()
results.notes: NostrSystem does not verify by default (checkSigs: false); the harness turns checkSigs on. Request options: groupingDelay: 0 (the option snort's own fetch() sets; by default Query.start waits groupingDelay = 100 ms on a setTimeout before it sends the REQ, to merge requests) and leaveOpen: true (the query is closed in teardown): with the default (false) a 30 s QueryFetchTimeout hard timer would cut a long stream, and the trace closes at the EOSE while the last events of the socket read that carried it still wait in the pool's queueMicrotask verify batch, so those are dropped (a tail of ~50 events lost, a different number every run). ConnectToRelay does not wait for the socket to open; setup waits until the pool's connection reports isOpen, so the handshake is untimed. Each connection also starts a NIP-11 fetch at connect (in parallel with the handshake, kept in a module-level cache). Unconditional library work: the Query delivers through its feed, a NoteCollection, a sorted in-memory store (a SortedMap insert with splice per event) that hands new events to "event" listeners on a timer (emitInterval 300 ms), so events reach the app up to 300 ms after the EOSE and the run ends at the last one. That store keeps one event per replaceable key (an older kind 0/3/1xxxx version is never delivered) and adds an event only if created_at > (stored.created_at ?? 0), so an event with created_at 0 is never delivered: on the corpus it drops valid events (accepted_ok false). The connection pool batches the events of one microtask turn into one optimizer.batchVerify call; verification checks the signature against an id it recomputes (EventExt.createId) but never compares it to event.id, so the harness also calls EventExt.createId(event) and drops events whose id differs (a second serialization + sha256 per event). "event" handlers receive arrays of new events. Other options default (the automatic outbox model only acts on filters with authors). A new NostrSystem per run. The published dist has extensionless relative ESM imports: on Node the harness registers a module-resolution hook (snort-resolve.mjs: retries .js and /index.js, as a bundler does) to load the unmodified package; Bun resolves them itself; Deno cannot load it.

results.websocket: the Rust SDK's own client: async-wsocket 0.17 over tokio-tungstenite 0.28 (native, on its tokio threads)
results.crypto: libsecp256k1 (C, secp256k1-sys 0.10.1 via the Rust secp256k1 0.30 crate, in the native addon; nostr 0.45.3, nostr-sdk 0.45.2)
results.notes: Native bindings (uniffi, napi) of the Rust nostr-sdk: socket, JSON parsing, id and signature verification run in Rust on its own threads; each delivered event crosses the FFI as an Event handle and the harness reads its id with event.id().toHex() (an FFI call). The stream ends at EOSE (ReqExitPolicy.ExitOnEose): its end is the EOSE; the timeout argument of streamEvents is left unset (none). It drops expired (NIP-40) events unconditionally. Deduplication across relays is by id. A new Client per run.
